decisions.reason: The question asks whether token-level highlighting helps users identify edits, but omits the explicit comparison between highlighting likely edits and highlighting low-probability tokens.
The poster states what the edit model predicts but omits the preliminary data from nine coders who corrected Codex outputs until the tasks were completed properly.

The poster reports 30 participants and three easy LeetCode tasks. It omits the participants’ employment context and Python experience, along with randomization of task order and tool-to-task assignments.

The poster identifies Davinci-002 Codex, all three conditions, and both thresholds. It omits that the thresholds matched total highlight counts across the three tasks for the two highlighting conditions.

The poster gives all three means with the correct conditions and distinguishes the significant advantage over Generation probability from the comparison with Prediction only. The figure caption states the 10-minute cap.

Panel (b) shows survival bars by condition and highlight status, with heights consistent with the checklist at the displayed resolution. The poster does not explicitly give the five values, define survival as a token remaining untouched, or connect the pattern to more localized editing.

Panel (c) shows higher preference for Edit model, with bar heights consistent with the checklist at the displayed resolution. The poster does not explicitly report the exact means, p-value, or survey item wording and reverse coding.
The poster omits that the edit model was trained on the evaluated completions and that comparable effects on unseen tasks remain unverified.
The poster omits that effects on the accuracy of human oversight and on automation bias remain untested.

notes: The figure caption correctly associates panels (a), (b), and (c) with task time, token survival, and preference. The inset axis labels, condition labels, and legend are small at the supplied resolution, and the bar heights support approximate comparisons only. The title and section headings make the reading order clear. Counts reflect observed errors. Missing scientific details are recorded in the checklist decisions.
